dataset.description: Household survey of Syrian refugees in four countries of asylum, covering displacement history, housing/land/property at origin, return intentions, employment, social cohesion, economic status and protection risks. One row per responding household per round, reported by a single adult respondent whose position on the roster is recorded in s2_1_hh_relationship_lbl. Countries of asylum: Egypt, Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon (46 governorates); areas of origin: 15 Syrian governorates. Fieldwork May-June 2025 over 67 distinct interview dates, with both round labels falling inside the same two-month window. Round 1 contributes 6,316 rows and round 2 contributes 4,033. The file carries no identifier that links a respondent across rounds -- panel_hh_key is the round tag and a row counter that restarts at zero each round -- so the two rounds are treated as independent cross-sections and every row is an independent respondent. Questions and routing are from the Round 1 and Round 2 CATI questionnaires, which are identical for the host-country sections; round 2 adds a module for households that had moved back to Syria, which no row in this file took. Three mutually exclusive conditional branches hang off the twelve-month return-intention item (s3_11): a return branch (s7a), a do-not-return branch (s7b) and an undecided branch (s7c). Preprocessing (v1.3): every variable is categorical with a declared set of levels. Ages, household member counts and calendar years, which the source file ships as free integers, are cut into closed bands whose terminal categories are top- and bottom-coded. Two items coded as bare numbers in round 1 and as prefixed labels in round 2 (s2_6_return_decision_maker, s4_3_main_earner_gender) carry the labels in both. A cell the routing never put to the respondent carries the gate sentinel: round 1 marks those cells with the CATI's own skip marker and round 2 leaves them empty, at item-by-item rates that agree to within about a percentage point. 156 of the 230 given and predicted items carry that marker somewhere and are gated; the rest never do and cannot be. One item, s3_5_family_in_syria_lbl, is left ungated and carries the ordinary level 'Not recorded' on its 53 empty cells, which are too few and too unstructured to read as routing. No cell is null: NaN means the cell is held out. Gates state the instrument's routing. Five of them approximate a condition the one-parent gate format cannot express and one is inferred from skip rates rather than from printed routing; all six are set out in GATE_CORRECTIONS.md. They are not a constraint the delivered rows satisfy: agreement between a gate and who actually holds a value has a median of 0.83 and ranges from 0.29 to 0.98, and the three branches off s3_11, which the instrument makes mutually exclusive, overlap in the file. In five multi-select families (6.4, 6.6, 6.11, 7A.7, 7B.1, 59 items) round 1 wrote 0 for respondents the routing skipped rather than marking them skipped at all, so for those items the sentinel appears on round-2 rows only.
